english: You approach the door.
Bookbinder? You got business here?
(Knock on the door.)
E-(Leave.)
That's fun. Didn't expect that, considering... everything. I'm not a big reader myself, but I indulge occasionally.
He sounds surprised.
That's rude. <shake>Very rude</shake>...
But it's just banter. You can handle it.
What, did you think I don't like books? I'm a professional and highly esoterically minded cleric. Of course I love books! (Be offended.)
What kind of wizard would dislike books? (Be a wizard.)
You can read?
Rogue.
Are you upset?
He cracks a smile.
Like, genuinely?
Pff. No.
Slightly. Yes.
You feel a bubbling brewing.
It is... rage.
NO.
Yeah, a bit.
(Make grumpy cleric noises.)
The goblin stifles a laugh.
He shrugs.
I mean, it's a stereotype. Figured you'd be more original than that.
So what, I'm an illiterate ape-wizard? Those haven't existed since the Fade Era!
What can I say? I'm boring.
I don't know about that, but...
I learn something new about you every minute it seems.
Fuck off.
Do you mean a note-sheet? Or... what?
I'm a dancing kind of bard, so... no.
But you just said...?
Nevermind that. I change my mind.
He groans.
I don't know, Cleric.
His sound makes it clear that he is tired of you talking about druidic things, despite the fact that he should celebrate your passionate love for nature.
...What?
I'm sorry?
Rogue. I'm a rogue.
I didn't ask!
Well. Maybe we shouldn't just stand here talking in front of a shop.
You knocking, or we leaving?
Within seconds of the knock, the slit on the door slides open.
Beyond you see a pair of large yellow eyes glaring at you.
Hey-o.
Bird.
Is this pest control?
The eyes quickly tilt to the left.
Tilt?
No.
Yes.
In a sense?
No...
The eyes push closer to the slit in the door. As they do, a bush of gray feathers pokes out.
A birdfolk.
Ah! An owl!
Hm? A cleric?
No, I'm a wizard.
No, I'm a rogue.
Yeah. Duh.
Hm.
The bird-man behind the door ruffles his feathers.
Shěn Yêlan is my name.
If you are not pest control, I need nothing from you. Please leave.
The hatch on the door swings open.
A pair of yellow piercing eyes gaze at you from beyond a veil of bushy feathers.
(Stick an AEFA into the deposit slot.) "From the Freestriders next-door."
You wanna go drink at the tavern later?
Are you a scholar?
E-"Thank you for your time."
So stern.
Good. He should keep working.
That is honorable.
A chat?
I did not think you were an animal speaking kind.
Oh well. You have my gratitude.
Half-off on future work!
Prayer book, yes? I have seen quite a few.
Drop inside, I will take check-a-look.
(Drop it in.)
Maybe later. I still need this broken mess.
Fine. What else?
Yes, yes. Horrible. Salt water. Left swollen.
You could have avoided the worst of this if the drying process had been handled better.
I will rebind this foul mess for you.
Great, thanks. (Turn to leave.)
How much will it cost?
Are you sure you can do it? It's pretty ruined.
One more thing. Before you run off.
We will see. It depends on the process.
Of course! What do you take me for?
I will need guidance on the direction of the rebinding.
The spells inside are lost, however the style and formatting can be saved.
Using my skills I can aim at something from the Towers. Which would be most similar to the original work.
I could also focus on rebinding it in the style of a druidic ledger. Or perhaps as a grimoire of the dark and forbidden arts.
Forbidden magic? Isn't that illegal? Hence the name.
You know druidic stuff?
Have you worked on many clerical tools?
Just remake it as well you can with the original intention in mind. (Choose an INTELLIGENCE upgrade.)
Make it a primal Druidic Ledger. (Choose a WISDOM upgrade.)
I want it to be full of forbidden magic. (Choose a CHARISMA upgrade.)
I am a registered spellcaster in your city.
He lets out an annoyed bird-sound.
That gives me the rights to handle any magical components and tools. No matter the outcome. As long as I do not cast it myself.
Thus is your law written.
That sounds like it could be abused.
Sounds profitable.
Uh...
It does, does it not?
It is indeed.
Make your decision.
I have many customers. Including the various druids of this city.
They have an aversion to modern practices themselves. Hence, my services are well-appreciated.
I am not an official merchant of the Towers, but many come to me for better prices and better service.
Despite how little most clerics enjoy working with my kin.
Yes. Most clerics are quite hateful against non-humans after all.
That's terrible. I'm not like those other clerics, I promise.
That is the way of the world. (Shrug.)
Indeed.
I do not care. I am not your friend.
Now, make a choice!
That I will do.
Return tomorrow. Not while the sun rises. I am either resting or working intently during those hours.
Anything else you want, or will you leave me to work?
And if you want it done faster, stop bothering me.
The owl beyond the door goes silent for a few seconds. His yellow eyes gazing at you.
Judgmental. That is what he looks like.
You... bêndân...
Do you suffer from memory loss?
Maybe in an esoteric sense. But no.
Oh right. I just turned the book in. Sorry.
The owl sighs.
Come back tomorrow. And consider seeing a professional for your erratic behavior.
All geniuses are called erratic at some point.
Perhaps you should.
Okay. Sorry to disturb you in your work.
What if I throw more money at you? Can you get it done quicker?
Yes, yes.
The owl grumbles beyond the door.
If you bake a bun in ten minutes on double the heat- you don't get it done faster. You get a burnt bun.
Don't burn my book!
I get it. I'll come back tomorrow.
If you leave now, I will consider it.
The owl-man goes quiet.
Ten... thousand?
Yeah.
You have ten thousand crowns?
...Well. If you do...
It would still take another hour. But...
(Toss in 10,000 crowns into the hole in the door.) "I'll wait an hour. Go fix it."
No. I was joking. (Keep your money.)
Sixty minutes pass.
Of course you were.
How wise of you.
Yes, yes. It is done now.
Now you pay.
Nice! How much do I owe you?
Payment? How much.
Right. Money. I have that.
The process was quite complicated, but I handled it like the pro I am.
The final cost is two hundred and fifty Norvikian crowns.
Oh boy. That's a fair amount for you.
Pay now.
You could purchase a basic spell book for fifty.
However, if this bird is as proficient as he believes himself to be, then it could be worth the cost.
Good. Now pay! Two-fifty.
Good. Now pay! One-hundred.
TWO HUNDRED AND FIFTY?!
Make him lower the price. Through pure charm.
...I'll come back later. Maybe.
CROWNS?!
That's reasonable.
That's a crazy high amount!
Good. Now pay.
No. You are wrong. It is very reasonable for this kind of job.
Damn. Should've said that other thing.
That is a bold assumption.
However, it is true my issues with those constant pests have gone away...
Even the little noises. Thus I have been able to rest properly for once...
Come on. I'm such a nice cleric.
I worked hard for it.
Please. I'm begging you.
Fine.
You get it for free. But only due to me not having to pay Pest Control now.
Helping people helps you! Nice!
You did not do it for gain. But it is nice nonetheless to be rewarded with knowledge.
No, you cannot.
Time to start hustling, if you wanna get that book back.
You pour in all 250 crowns from your Pouch of Holding. And...
You toss in all 100 crowns from your Pouch of Holding. And...
You gotta comb his feathers, you know?
Just say-
Make it a hundred and I'll owe you big time. Wouldn't it be nice to have a cleric in your debt?
True.
Okay, pay hundred. Then you get your book.
Nice! That's a BIG discount!
Alas, since you're so FUCKING POOR - you still can't afford it.
Easy. Just say-
Can you lower the price?
Shit. Worth a try.
You better. Book stays with me until you do.
Out of the slot in the door you see the end of a paper-wrapped book.
Take it.
(Take it.)
You open the wrap- discovering one of the most beautiful and intricately crafted tomes you have ever seen.
The inside is filled with arcane runes, the like of which you can use in your work.
A masterpiece of a spell book. Never let this one fall into the river.
You open the wrap- discovering a wildly bound book, its paper smelling like a fresh damp forest.
Yet it is easy to use, opening it reveals a series of Primal patterns.
It is quite frankly a masterpiece of esoteric delight.
You open the wrap- discovering a book that feels eerie to the touch.
The inside is marked by some fiendish geometric shapes, along with various arcane shortcuts...
A masterpiece! You'll love using this as your spell book, won't you?
It feels tingly to your touch.
Extremely esoteric.
You are happy. I can see it.
The yellow eyes tilt to the side as they peer at you from the slot.
Now be on your way. And mention my services to your clerical friends. I am the BEST, you see. That needs to be known.
Will do, general... (Stare at your new book.)
(Just nod.)
Anything else before you leave? No?
I see. I have heard of this.
It will be considered. Anything else?
Another one delivered. Hells yes.
You are interested in the arts.
It's kind of my job, yeah.
I'd love to hear more about you. An owlkin in Norvik is not so common.
If you have anything to share, let's hear it.
I was trained in the Knowledge, back in Three Wings. I know many things.
But no time to talk or share. Busy. If you want scholarly teachings, go speak with my upstairs neighbor.
That gnome never stops talking.
Just go upstairs. His door is always open.
You know him. Good.
And I will not learn the differences between gnomes and halflings for the same reason you people will call my kind birdfolk, clumping us together with the foul feathers of the darker bands.
Racism.
Logic.
Fear, mostly.
Self-preservation.
Spite.
What reason is that?
Sounds kind of petty.
Understandable.
Spite.
Told you.
Yes. It is.
Yes. Yes it is.
Rats!
Oh.
They are awful. Keep spawning out of the sewer pipes.
Yeah, the PCG should really take care of that.
Yes!
He lets out an angry bird-noise.
But that bastard guild leader, Tor-Lim Slip keeps telling me they don't have time.
No TIME?
They have a dozen teams running around the city. No TIME...
I've heard the big problem is that they cannot get anyone to do Pest Control missions at one star levels.
The PCG has a ranking system based on the danger of any particular pest they handle.
One-star?
Of course. Rats would be a one-star problem.
Yeah, they've got a whole ranking system.
The Halfways- we haven't relied on the PCG for years. They just don't have time for anything under a two-star danger ranking.
It is VERY annoying.
I have looked into it, and the problem is: the Pest Control teams that join the guild only take on one-star missions for a couple of weeks.
Then they quickly start focusing ONLY on the higher-paying tasks. And all the actual normal pests keep on spreading throughout the city...
It is a ridiculously IDIOTIC system.
So while all the mimics and monsters keep getting slayed, nothing is done about these darn RATS!
Your scarf nudges up against your left ear and whispers, "Meek think people in not-dungeon dislike mimic."
Meek kind of gets it. But still is not fun to hear.
The Pest Control Guild uses a legendarily poor design.
Like, actually really inefficient.
Entirely due to it being a public thing of course. Had it been privatized from the start...
The problem is it's too privatized. If the city held full control of all PEST CONTROL, then even the less valuable missions would be handled.
Obviously.
So Urth would personally go into the sewer to stomp on rats, you say?
YES.
If so necessary, YES.
The bird takes a few breaths after his rant.
Worst part: my nephew has a team himself. The White Doves they're called.
And I've tried sending messages to him also. But he just says the same thing!
Too busy... too busy...
I could join the Pest Control Guild.
Tell me more about your nephew.
I could take a look at it. It does kind of sound like a quest.
Well. Good luck with that. (Think about it.)
The owl-man scoffs.
Sure, and then you'd go and take on all the big and scary monsters that crawl up into the city.
Ignoring all the actual pests. Just to get a payday.
Yes, that does sound like exactly what I'd do.
No way. I'd work my ass off trudging through the sewers, catching rats, for a barely-nothing payout. All for the satisfaction of a hard day's work.
Of course.
Really?
...Probably not actually.
Yes. I'm that good of a guy.
Well, if everyone was like you, this city would be a better place.
He calls himself Valerian Windrider. That is... the Norvikian way of saying his name.
He's also active within that Freestrider party, if you're interested in throwing a vote for one of my fellow owl-kin.
He works with one of those filthy Yobus, which I am not happy about. Oh, and a halfling. A cleric, in fact. Of the Lady Fair church.
That's interesting. Thank you for telling me about them.
They sound sketchy.
Ah. I've heard of that church. Over in Housing, right?
You are welcome.
I will not disagree.
That's the one. I think they're connected with an orphanage.
Hm. If you do, I would be very happy.
The rats seem to come from the sewers, connected with the City Below.
Thank you.
